The test image shows a **stem** with dark brown-to-black discoloration and dead wilted leaves. The stem lesion is extensive and very dark. There's a small whitish area at the node. Stem candidates: Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers, Gray_Mold, Southern_Blight, Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato.

Now viewing one reference from each of my top 4 candidates:

**Analysis:**

- **Test image**: Stem with extensive dark brown to almost black discoloration, completely dead/desiccated leaves hanging above the lesion, small whitish material at the leaf node junction. Healthy green leaves on surrounding plant.

**Reference comparisons:**
- **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers** (5530065): Shows dark brown-black canker at soil line — matches the very dark stem color in test image.
- **Gray_Mold** (5528796): Shows tan/light brown stem lesion — too light, doesn't match the near-black darkness.
- **Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato** (5368890): Shows internal vascular cracking when stem cut open — doesn't match external appearance.
- **Southern_Blight** (1575059): Shows dark black lower stem + bleached white area — partially similar, but usually at soil line with white mycelial mats.

**Conclusion:** The very dark (near-black) stem lesion causing girdling and complete leaf desiccation above the lesion is the hallmark of Alternaria stem canker. The description matches: "large, irregularly shaped, dark-brown to almost black cankers... enlarging to cause girdled stems, stem death." Gray Mold is lighter tan/brown. Southern Blight would show white mycelial mats at soil line.
